page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-16GB is a cloud server instance provisioned on the KVM hypervisor within the Cloud Native family. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz, providing 2 shared vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 1 thread per core. The processor allocation features 64 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache, supporting instruction sets including AVX, AES-NI, SHA-NI, and BMI2, while lacking AVX-512 extensions. The server is allocated 16.0 GB of system memory, establishing a generous ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU core. It includes no bundled local storage, no hardware GPU accelerators, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark assessments reveal polarized performance characteristics between single-thread execution and concurrent compute tasks. In synthetic evaluation, the instance achieves an upper-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2243.0 and a strong text processing score of 2793.0. Conversely, sustained throughput metrics indicate bottlenecks associated with shared CPU resource distribution. Stress-ng records single-core performance of 771.48 and multi-core performance of 1555.48, both falling in the bottom decile. Similarly, PassMark CPU benchmarks register 4048.74, and multi-core Geekbench reaches 4156.0. Memory throughput provides 33.08 GB/sec uncached sequential read speed and 26.54 GB/sec write speed, supporting 2.91 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.34 GB/sec static web serving throughput.

The primary architectural tradeoff centers on high memory capacity combined with shared, low-concurrency CPU resources and absence of local disk. From an infrastructure cost perspective, this offers an economical footprint for workloads requiring elevated memory footprints without heavy compute demands. UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-16GB is best suited for memory-centric microservices, background task workers, text parsing utilities, and lightweight in-memory caching layers that utilize attached network block storage.
description: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-2xCPU-16GB is a memory-oriented virtual instance built on the KVM hypervisor, powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor running at 2.0 GHz. Configured with 2 shared x86_64 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, it maintains an elevated memory density of 8.0 GB per core. The server includes no integrated local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance demonstrates strong single-core Geekbench performance of 2243.0 and competent small LLM text generation at 102.29 tokens per second, though multi-threaded throughput tests like stress-ng and PassMark show lower compute capacity under sustained load. Memory write bandwidth stands at 26.54 GB/sec, supporting Redis workloads at 2.91 million operations per second. With its high RAM-to-CPU ratio and shared CPU model, this server is suitable for lightweight in-memory caches, text processing applications, and memory-dependent auxiliary services requiring external storage volumes.
